prompt: Combine two Consumers so both run in order on every accepted value, and build a Consumer that appends accepted strings to a sink list. Complete both methods in Consumers, then run the tests.
explanation: A Consumer<T> takes a value and returns nothing, so combining two of them just means calling accept on each in sequence inside a new lambda -- exactly what the built-in andThen default method does. appendTo shows that a lambda can capture the sink list from the enclosing method and keep using it long after appendTo returned; the method reference sink::add is the shortest way to write it.
hints: In both, return a lambda: value -> { a.accept(value); b.accept(value); }.
Order matters -- the tests log which consumer ran first, so call a before b.
appendTo can capture the sink parameter: return x -> sink.add(x), or simply sink::add.
